hints: Focus on what type of compound splits to give a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol on hydrolysis.
Work backwards from propanoic acid, its acyl part must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$, so look for an ester starting that way.
Now match the alcohol part, propan-2-ol needs the group $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$ joined through oxygen, so put the two halves together.
walkthrough:
**Spot the ester hydrolysis pattern**

Great start, remember that an ester plus water gives a carboxylic acid plus an alcohol. Think of it as splitting at the COO link.

$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH + R'OH}$$

**Build the two halves you need**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, so the acyl side RCO must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}$. Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, so the alkyl side R' must be $\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$.

**Join them to make the ester**

Just join the acid part to the alcohol part with loss of water, acid minus OH plus alcohol minus H. That gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$, which is isopropyl propanoate.

options.A: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. The acid side is correct for propanoic acid, but the alcohol side is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{OH}$, which is 2-methylpropan-1-ol, not propan-2-ol.
options.B: This is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Hydrolysis gives $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{CHCOOH}$ (2-methylpropanoic acid) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ (ethanol). Students pick this by mixing up which side is branched.
options.C: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. Splitting at the ester link gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (propanoic acid) and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ (propan-2-ol). Perfect match for both products.
options.D: This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_3$. The alcohol side is correct for propan-2-ol, but the acid side is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (butanoic acid), which has one carbon too many.
